diagnoses: reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md lacks explicit, hard requirements about deliverables and task completion conditions: it does not enumerate the five required output files (/app/output/q01.json .. q05.json), their exact schemas, or a final self-check gate. The location hint points specifically at '交付物和任务完成条件' (deliverables and completion conditions) in this file.

The toolkit SKILL.md's 'Minimal end-to-end scaffold' stops at 'Write outputs into /app/output' without naming q01..q05 files or asserting their existence/schema conformance before finishing, so an agent following only this skill may skip or misname outputs.

The toolkit SKILL.md does not state the completion contract (all 5 files must exist, be valid JSON, match the per-question schema, floats rounded to 2 decimals, arrays sorted by run_id/board_family/board_id ascending, null for missing). These acceptance conditions are only partially present and scattered under 'Output construction guardrails'.

Q4 guidance inside the toolkit is ambiguous about which direction 'required_min_speed_cm_min' encodes and how 'meets' is evaluated; it offers two formulas without tying them to the schema field used by the task, risking inverted meets logic as a completion-condition defect.
Q5 completion conditions (best run per board_family, runner_up_run_ids content/sorting) are not described at all in the toolkit SKILL.md, leaving the deliverable undefined.
repair_plan: In reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md, add an explicit 'Deliverables' section listing the exact file paths /app/output/q01.json through /app/output/q05.json, stating all five MUST be written (even with null values) for the task to be considered complete.

Add a 'Task completion conditions' checklist to the toolkit SKILL.md: (a) all 5 files exist and are valid JSON, (b) schemas match the per-question schema exactly (keys, nesting, types), (c) floats rounded to 2 decimals right before serialization, (d) arrays sorted ascending by run_id / board_family / board_id as specified, (e) null used for missing values (never NaN/Inf), (f) IDs serialized as strings, (g) every threshold is traceable to a handbook passage.

Extend the 'Minimal end-to-end scaffold' to show writing each of q01..q05 with json.dump(..., indent=2) and a final assertion loop that checks file existence and json.loads round-trip before the agent finishes.

Clarify Q4 completion semantics: define required_min_speed_cm_min as the handbook-derived speed threshold the actual conveyor speed must satisfy, and specify the exact direction of the 'meets' comparison consistent with the handbook (document the chosen inequality in a comment and keep both candidate formulas but mark which one maps to the schema field).

Add a short Q5 deliverable spec: one entry per board_family, best_run_id chosen by compliance-first then handbook-defined quality/efficiency tiebreak, runner_up_run_ids = remaining run_ids in that family sorted ascending as strings.
Preserve all existing deterministic computation recipes (sorting, slope, time-above-threshold, sensor tie-breaks, Q02 min-TAL representative rule, peak/margin, rounding helper) verbatim.
preservation_constraints: Do not modify reflow-machine-maintenance-guidance/SKILL.md or skilltta-task-guidance/SKILL.md beyond what is necessary; the location hint only targets the toolkit SKILL.md.
Preserve the Q02 representative-sensor invariant (minimum TAL across TCs with lexicographic tc_id tiebreak, status derived from that selected record) exactly as written.
Keep the handbook-grounding principle: no guessed thresholds; all limits traced to handbook.pdf.
Preserve existing code snippets for max_slope_in_temp_band, time_above_threshold_s, r2 rounding, sorting/de-dup rules, and sensor tie-break logic.
